title: Andal's garland
hookLine: a girl tries on the garland meant for the god
carry: bhakti: love is the real offering

cards: A garland of fresh flowers lies ready in a temple gardener's house, woven that morning for the image of Vishnu. While her father is out, his daughter picks it up and puts it around her own neck.
Then she looks at her reflection and asks: would he want me? The he, for her, is the god the garland was made for. Today we meet the people who sang Krishna's story, in the Tamil south.

teach.h: THE ALVARS: POETS SUNK DEEP IN GOD.
teach.b: The Alvars are the poet-saints of Vishnu who sang in Tamil. Tradition counts twelve, and explains the name as people sunk deep in God. Their songs are love songs, complaints, lullabies, longing.
The girl with the garland is one of them: Andal. Her father, himself remembered as one of the Alvars, tends a flower garden for the temple.

teach.h: A BABY UNDER THE TULASI PLANT.
teach.b: Tradition says he found her there as a baby, under a tulasi plant, and raised her as his own. She grows up on Krishna's stories and will marry no one but the Lord.

teach.h: HER FATHER THROWS THE GARLAND OUT.
teach.b: So she wears the garland before it goes to the temple. One day her father catches her. He's horrified: a garland someone has worn can't be offered to God.
He throws it out and weaves a new one. That night, the story says, the Lord comes to him in a dream and asks why the usual garland didn't arrive.

teach.h: THE ONE SHE WORE IS THE ONE HE WANTS.
teach.b: The one she wore is the one he wants. From then on her garlands go to the temple after she's worn them, and she's called the girl who gave the garland she had worn. In Hindu worship the offering goes to God first.
Flowers, food, a garland: you don't taste it, sniff it or try it on. Afterward it comes back to you as prasad, blessed, and you take it with both hands.
Andal's story runs that order backward, and the tradition loves her for it. It didn't change the rule; families still offer fresh. But it shows what the rule is for.
This is bhakti, the heart of the Alvars: what the Lord wants is love, and love is the real offering. Nammalvar, the other great Alvar, comes the day after tomorrow.

how: Andal is honored as one of the Alvars in Sri Vaishnava temples and homes; at Srivilliputtur, tradition holds that a garland worn by her image is still offered to the Lord.

practice: Before your next meal or drink, do what many Hindu families do. Set it down and offer it first, silently, to Krishna, or to God by whatever name you use. Then eat it as prasad, a gift given back to you.
If you don't pray, pause for one breath of thanks before the first bite.
